selection_reason: Classic theoretical basis for pore surface relaxation, restricted diffusion and the interpretation of T2 in terms of pore size.

Key background on inverting multi-exponential decay / CPMG data with non-negative least-squares methods; supports the statement that the inversion is ill-posed and needs constraints or regularization.
Theoretical review of NMR in porous media, T2/T2 and the interpretation of pore coupling.
Theoretical background on the interpretation of T2 distributions, diffusion and surface relaxation in complex pore systems such as carbonates.
Idealized pore geometry / triangular-pore model and its simulation; useful for showing how geometry affects the T2 spectrum.
Diffusion regimes and the interpretation of the NMR response; supplements the physical background on diffusion limitation and coupling in simulation results.
Theoretical background on interpreting the NMR response in terms of hydrological and porous-media parameters.
Book chapters by Dunn et al. on surface relaxation, multi-exponential decay and the mechanisms of NMR in porous media.
Standard NMR petrophysics textbook; a source for basic concepts, the interpretation of T2 distributions and application context.
Random-walk pore-scale forward simulation of NMR; directly supports the interpretation of simulated decays and T2 distributions.
General random-walk method for simulating the pore-scale NMR response.
Effects of temperature and diffusive coupling on the NMR response; useful for explaining peak broadening and peak shifts.
Monte Carlo / random-walk simulation of the NMR response; supports the forward-inversion chain.
Diffusive coupling mixes the signals of different pore populations; an important basis for interpreting merged peaks and changes in spectral shape.
Random-walk simulation of pore coupling in carbonates; supports the interpretation of T2 spectra for complex pore structures.
Simulation background on random walks and diffusive coupling; useful for explaining how pore-scale connectivity affects the spectral shape.
Link between diffusive coupling, T2 distributions and rock-type interpretation in simulation and interpretation.
Pore-scale random-walk / restricted-diffusion simulation; useful when comparing inverted spectra with the true pore structure.
Numerical simulation of the multidimensional NMR response; background for T2/T1-T2/T2-T2 simulation.
Classic simulation reference for the NMR / diffusion theory in restricted geometries.
Early random-walk method; background supporting the choice of Monte Carlo simulation.
Strong theoretical background on diffusion / random walks; a supplement for deeper theory.
Effect of field inhomogeneity / internal gradients on the NMR response; can explain sources of mismatch between simulation and inversion.
Conference paper on pore-scale / random-walk simulation; a methodological supplement.
Finite-volume method and internal-gradient effects; useful for explaining the influence of boundary conditions and gradients in numerical models.
Background on FEM forward simulation; supports the interpretation of finite-element methods.
Finite-element modelling of the NMR response; closely related to the simulation-inversion interpretation in this project.
Pore-scale numerical simulation; background on internal gradients and surface relaxation.
Simulation and inversion interpretation for T2-T2 and related two-dimensional NMR; supports the interpretation of pore coupling and spectral shape.
Simulation of diffusion and relaxation in restrictive geometries; useful for interpreting idealized pore simulations.
Practical background on COMSOL / FEM modelling; a reference for reproducing numerical model setups.
Background on LBM / pore-scale NMR simulation; suitable for comparison with random-walk and FEM approaches.
Foundations of the lattice Boltzmann method; supports the interpretation of LBM simulations.
Matrix diagonalization / eigenmode methods; supports understanding of analytical and semi-analytical forward modelling.
Simulation background on matrix methods and the effect of saturation and drainage conditions on the NMR response.
Paper on matrix diagonalization methods; supplements the eigenvalue / eigenmode interpretation.
Numerical simulation of two-dimensional NMR and fluid identification; suitable for extending to multidimensional response interpretation.
Numerical background on the echo-train / CPMG response; a reference for decay generation and pre-inversion processing.
Short review of pore coupling and the interpretation of multi-peak spectra; suitable for citing in result discussion.
Combines experiment and interpretation with a focus on pore coupling; useful for interpreting simulated spectral shapes.
Pore coupling and the interpretation of T2 distributions; a bridge between simulation results and experimental observations.
Interpretation of T2/T2 and related two-dimensional NMR; supports the analysis of complex spectral shapes and peak groups.
Background on two-dimensional NMR and the interpretation of pore fluids; suitable for extending the result discussion.
Background on T2-T2 and the interpretation of pore coupling / exchange.
Background on the interpretation of T2-T2 / multidimensional NMR; supports the interpretation of complex T2 spectra.
Background on the T2-T2 method and spectral interpretation.
Original reference for the L-curve method: the L-shaped curve of residual norm versus solution (semi)norm, and the relation between its corner and the choice of the regularization parameter.
Classic reference on interpreting relaxation data as a spectrum of relaxation times by least squares / linear programming; states explicitly that the solution is non-unique.
Shows that a fixed smoothing coefficient broadens sharp peaks or splits a broad peak or tail into spurious multiple peaks, and proposes locally variable smoothing (UPEN).

Measured T2 as a function of static field strength and CPMG pulse spacing: surface relaxation dominates at low field and short spacing, while diffusion in the gradient appears at high field and long spacing.

Summarizes the relaxation mechanisms of pore fluids in rock: surface paramagnetic ions dominate, in the fast-diffusion regime the relaxation spectrum maps onto the S/V spectrum, and typical values of T1/T2 and surface relaxivity are given.

Using synthetic calcium silicate powders with known iron/manganese concentrations, shows that surface relaxivity increases linearly with paramagnetic ion concentration and that oxide surfaces without paramagnetic ions still have appreciable relaxivity.

Analyses diffusion decay caused by internal gradients from susceptibility contrasts with the effective-gradient concept: only the decay in large pores increases markedly with echo spacing, and the effective gradient has an upper limit.
Quartz sand coated with five iron oxides; quantitatively compares surface relaxivity and internal-gradient effects, directly relevant to unconsolidated geological materials.
